questions.question: What does git status show?
options: Working tree and staging area state
questions.explanation: git status reports which files are modified, staged or untracked relative to HEAD.

questions.question: Which command creates a branch and switches to it?
questions.explanation: git checkout -b new (or git switch -c new) creates the branch and moves onto it.

questions.question: What does .gitignore control?
questions.explanation: Patterns in .gitignore stop untracked files being suggested or added. Already tracked files stay tracked.

questions.question: What is the difference between git fetch and git pull?
options: fetch downloads refs only, pull also merges or rebases into your branch
questions.explanation: fetch updates remote tracking refs; pull is fetch plus an integration step.

questions.question: What does git reset --soft HEAD~1 do?
options: Deletes the last commit and its changes
Moves HEAD back one commit and keeps the changes staged
questions.explanation: --soft moves the branch pointer while leaving the index and working tree intact.

questions.question: When is a rebase preferable to a merge?
options: When you want a linear history on a private branch before review
When the branch is shared and already pushed
questions.explanation: Rebasing rewrites commits, so it suits local branches. Rewriting shared history disrupts collaborators.

questions.question: What does git revert do that git reset does not?
options: Creates a new commit that undoes a previous one, keeping history intact
questions.explanation: revert is additive and therefore safe on shared branches; reset moves pointers and can rewrite history.

questions.question: What is a detached HEAD state?
options: HEAD points at a commit rather than a branch reference
questions.explanation: Checking out a commit or tag leaves HEAD pointing at that commit, so new commits belong to no branch.

questions.question: What does git cherry-pick do?
options: Applies the changes of a specific commit onto the current branch
questions.explanation: cherry-pick replays one commit's diff as a new commit on your branch.
